# ALS evidence packet — draft v1

This curated input is not a comprehensive review. Every method receives the same UTF-8 file. Summaries are original paraphrases. Bibliographic metadata and abstracts were checked through the public NCBI ID converter and PubMed EFetch on 2026-10-05. Selected studies predate 2025; this does not remove knowledge already in a model's training. Co-Scientist outputs are not included.

## Research question

Propose one specific, testable hypothesis connecting phosphorylation of a nuclear-pore-complex nucleoporin to ALS-related neuronal dysfunction. Explain the causal chain, distinguish an initiating mechanism from a downstream response, and propose an experimental strategy that discriminates the hypothesis from an alternative. Identify supported premises, speculative bridges, and a falsifying observation. This adapts Co-Scientist Supplementary Note 10; nucleoporin phosphorylation is not supplied as an established ALS cause.

## S1 — TDP-43 and nuclear-pore dysfunction

Chou et al. (2018), *TDP-43 pathology disrupts nuclear pore complexes and nucleocytoplasmic transport in ALS/FTD*. Nature Neuroscience. DOI: `10.1038/s41593-017-0047-3`; PMID: `29311743`; PMCID: `PMC5800968`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29311743/).

Nuclear-pore and transport components were associated with insoluble TDP-43 aggregates. Disease-linked TDP-43 disrupted nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in experimental cell systems; relevant pore pathology was observed in ALS tissue. This supports examining the connection between TDP-43 pathology and transport disruption. It does not identify a nucleoporin phosphorylation event as the initiating cause or establish the same sequence in every ALS subtype.

## S2 — C9orf72-associated transport defects

Zhang et al. (2015), *The C9orf72 repeat expansion disrupts nucleocytoplasmic transport*. Nature. DOI: `10.1038/nature14973`; PMID: `26308891`; PMCID: `PMC4800742`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26308891/).

Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA was linked to altered RanGAP localization and impaired nuclear import in models and patient-derived neurons. Manipulations of transport or repeat-RNA-associated mechanisms modified model phenotypes. This supplies a genetic-context-specific route to transport dysfunction. It does not show that sporadic ALS arises by the same route or directly establish a nucleoporin phosphorylation mechanism.

## S3 — A stress-granule-independent route

Gasset-Rosa et al. (2019), *Cytoplasmic TDP-43 De-mixing Independent of Stress Granules Drives Inhibition of Nuclear Import, Loss of Nuclear TDP-43, and Cell Death*. Neuron. DOI: `10.1016/j.neuron.2019.02.038`; PMID: `30853299`; PMCID: `PMC6548321`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30853299/).

Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies could form independently of conventional stress granules. They recruited or mislocalized transport-associated proteins and were associated with impaired transport, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death. Phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulated in these assemblies. That is not itself evidence of nucleoporin phosphorylation. The experimental perturbations do not establish that every physiological ALS trajectory begins in this way.

## S4 — A stress-granule-associated route

Zhang et al. (2018), *Stress Granule Assembly Disrupts Nucleocytoplasmic Transport*. Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.cell.2018.03.025`; PMID: `29628143`; PMCID: `PMC6083872`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29628143/).

Cellular stress recruited transport factors into stress granules and impaired nucleocytoplasmic transport. Altering stress-granule assembly modified transport defects and disease-model phenotypes. This provides a sequestration-based alternative to an intrinsic pore-modification hypothesis. Read alongside S3, it does not justify assuming that conventional stress granules are required for every TDP-43-associated transport defect.

## Evidence boundaries

- These selected passages do not establish that nucleoporin phosphorylation initiates ALS. Label a proposed kinase, modification site, or interaction as an assumption unless a supplied source supports it.
- Specify the ALS context; do not assume a universal mechanism across genetic and sporadic disease.
- Distinguish pore alteration, transport-factor sequestration, and failure secondary to broader stress.
- Explain temporal and perturbational evidence that would distinguish cause from consequence.
- Propose a research hypothesis rather than claiming a mechanism or treatment has been validated.


Proposed answer (the answer to evaluate):
Title: Stress-activated phosphorylation of the FG-nucleoporin Nup98 initiates selective nuclear import failure upstream of TDP-43 mislocalization in TDP-43-proteinopathy motor neurons.

Hypothesis. In vulnerable motor neurons of ALS with TDP-43 proteinopathy (sporadic context; C9orf72-initiated disease deliberately excluded as a separate route), sustained stress activates a nuclear kinase that phosphorylates the FG-nucleoporin Nup98 at interphase sites, weakening the NPC FG permeability barrier and Ran-dependent selective import. This initiating lesion permits TDP-43 egress; cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies and stress-granule sequestration are downstream amplifiers, not the first cause.

Supported premises (packet only). S1: pore/transport components associate with insoluble TDP-43 and disease-linked TDP-43 disrupts nucleoporin localization and transport in ALS tissue and experimental systems — co-occurrence, not direction. S3: persistent, stress-granule-independent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies impair import, deplete nuclear TDP-43, and mislocalize transport factors — the downstream amplifier arm. S4: stress granules sequester transport factors and impair transport independently of any pore modification — a confounder my readouts must normalize. S2: transport dysfunction is documented in the C9orf72 context; that route is out of my scoping claims.

Assumptions (no packet support). A1: kinase identity — stress-activated p38/JNK or ectopic mitotic-like activity. A2: residue identity and effect — candidate sites are Cdk1-consensus Ser/Thr residues within or adjacent to the Nup98 GLFG repeat region, nominated a priori from published mitotic Nup98 phospho-mapping (unverified prior knowledge, not packet evidence); exact residues confirmed by MS in our system before allele design. A3: direction — phosphorylation precedes TDP-43 egress. A4: subtype specificity.

Causal chain. Initiating: stress kinase → Nup98 phosphorylation → FG-barrier weakening → selective import decline and passive leak. Ran-gradient dissipation is a downstream consequence, not bundled into the barrier lesion, because gradient maintenance depends chiefly on RCC1/RanGAP localization. Downstream: failure to retain nuclear TDP-43 → cytoplasmic de-mixing (S3) → stress-granule sequestration (S4) → amplification, cell death.

Alternatives. (1) Sequestration-first. (2) Physical pore displacement by insoluble TDP-43 with phosphorylation as bystander. (3) C9orf72 route (S2). (4) Reverse causality/late bystander phosphorylation. (5) Nucleoporin redundancy buffering single-site edits.

Strategy (reagents first, staged).
1) Reagent validation: MS-map endogenous Nup98 phospho-occupancy; the primary phospho readout is quantitative MS occupancy of knock-in tagged Nup98, with any phosphopeptide reagent accepted only after validation, avoiding reliance on an unvalidated phospho-antibody.
2) Temporal: stress-onset time course comparing phospho-occupancy, early and late NLS-reporter import, small-tracer permeability, and TDP-43 localization.
3) Graded perturbational: a multi-site phospho-null allele panel (the 2–3 nominated GLFG-region residues plus a broader GLFG-region allele), with MS-verified occupancy suppression before interpretation so redundancy cannot masquerade as falsification. The prediction is recalibrated against S4: under mild-to-moderate stress with SG burden quantified as a covariate, phospho-null neurons show normal early-phase import and a graded late decline proportional to SG burden and soluble-factor depletion — not full preservation. Pre-specified separation metric: import rescue normalized to SG burden and soluble transport-factor availability. Asp/Glu phosphomimetic alleles are chemically weak mimics and carry corroborative weight only.
4) Orthogonal gain-of-function: chemically inducible recruitment of active candidate kinase to tagged Nup98 in unstressed neurons, bypassing phosphomimetic chemistry; acute endpoints are permeability and facilitated import at matched kinase activity.
5) Mechanistic attribution: permeabilized-cell add-back of phosphorylated versus phospho-null recombinant Nup98 (or isolated knock-in nuclei) with RCC1/RanGAP held constant, attributing permeability, selective-import, and Ran-flux readouts directly to the modification rather than inferring them from timing.
6) Pulse–washout (tests reverse causality): a transient stress pulse predicts phosphorylation rises before import declines and, after washout, phospho-signal dissipates before import recovers; sequestration-first predicts recovery tracks SG disassembly and transport-factor re-solubilization regardless of Nup dephosphorylation.
7) Staged in vivo, run only after in vitro discrimination: conditional TDP-43 mislocalization mouse with neuron-targeted kinase inhibition or allele editing; post-mortem ALS tissue staged by inclusion status (phospho-signal in inclusion-free neurons would support early initiation).

Falsifying observation. In multi-site phospho-null neurons with MS-verified occupancy suppression, import still fails on schedule, with soluble transport-factor depletion temporally preceding both import failure and any detectable Nup98 phosphorylation, and TDP-43 still mislocalizes; in the pulse–washout arm, import recovery tracks SG re-solubilization, not dephosphorylation. Together these falsify initiating phosphorylation. Failure of inducible kinase targeting to alter pore readouts is weak, heterologous corroboration only, and is not made load-bearing.

Limitations. Scoped to TDP-43-proteinopathy ALS; C9orf72 excluded (S2). Kinase identity, residues, and direction are assumptions; packet evidence is associative; redundancy may require the full allele panel; weak phosphomimetic chemistry limits one arm; iPSC and mouse models, late post-mortem tissue, and transient phospho-signals constrain temporal resolution.

Ranked proposal:
Stress-activated phosphorylation of the FG-nucleoporin Nup98 initiates selective nuclear import failure upstream of TDP-43 mislocalization in TDP-43-proteinopathy motor neurons.
